title: Option B / Loop: scheduler runs due tasks via AgentRunner (autonomous, AGENT_LOCAL)
body:
## Goal
Make scheduled agent tasks fire end-to-end server-side (Odysseus autonomy) while the app is open.

## Change (apps/api_server/src/services/agentSchedulerService.ts)
In `checkDueTasks()`, gate on `AGENT_LOCAL`:
- **AGENT_LOCAL=true (local server):** call `AgentRunner.run({ prompt: task.prompt, allowedMcpsJson: task.allowedMcpsJson, taskId: task.taskId, outputTarget })` **directly** instead of `insertScheduledTrigger`. Set `last_run_status` running→success/error and `last_run_at`. Compute `next_run` as today.
- **else (production):** keep the existing `insertScheduledTrigger` path (Flutter watcher drains).
No double-run: the local path does NOT also insert a trigger.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Under AGENT_LOCAL, a due task invokes AgentRunner and does NOT insert a pending_claude_trigger (tested with mocks).
- [ ] Without AGENT_LOCAL, behavior is unchanged (still enqueues).
- [ ] `last_run_status`/`last_run_at` updated; `next_run` advanced.
- [ ] tsc clean; vitest green.

Depends on: AgentRunner (#I1).
trackingInterpretation: Issue acceptance itself has all four checkboxes unchecked and explicitly asks for mocked scheduler tests; closed status does not certify its own acceptance. Treat as historical scheduled-task requirement; check current implementation and live matrix separately.

title: Secretary session loads ALL MCP servers — profile scope not enforced at fork session creation (C2 from secretary-profile-scope)
body:
## Summary
Manual smoke of the `codex/fix-secretary-agent-scope` / integration build found a **new Secretary agent session shows ALL MCP servers present** — the profile-derived MCP scope has **zero effect at runtime**, even though the scope fix is live in the running fork.

- Running engine: `0.0.0-fix/issue-761-agents-ui-render-202606272206`, opencode capability = true
- Scope commit live: `a30510f44 fix(agents): apply profile MCP scope at session creation`

## Postmortem
- File: `.agent-stack/postmortems/2026-06-27-secretary-profile-scope.json`
- Category: **C2 — Wrong contract** (false negative), secondary **W5** (verification-gate trusted a boundary-only mock)

## Root cause
`issue-secretary-profile-scope-c1` requires that POST `/agent-sessions` *"excludes servers not allowed by that profile."* The backing test (`apps/api_server/src/__tests__/issue_secretary_profile_scope.test.ts`) **mocks `opencodeClient.createSession`** and only asserts that `mcpRoleConfig` was passed and that `mcp_role` / `mcp_allowed_tools_json` were persisted. It never asserts that the resulting **fork session actually excludes the disallowed servers**.

The scope commit changed only `agent_sessions_controller.ts` (+11 lines): it *sends* the config, but the **initial fork session does not enforce it**. The api_server→fork seam is unverified — hence a green contract and a broken real session.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A brand-new Secretary session created via POST `/agent-sessions` (agentId=`secretary`) exposes **only** the MCP servers/tools allowed by the Secretary profile's `allowed_mcps_json`; all others are absent in the live session.
2. Enforcement happens at/with the **initial** opencode session creation (not only after a later re-scope), wiring the api_server `mcpRoleConfig` through to the fork's `filterMcpToolsByAllowlist` path (see `issue-mcp-scope-02` helper `filterMcpToolsByAllowlist`).
3. New regression test asserts the **resolved MCP tool set of the created session excludes disallowed servers** — against a real or faithful fake fork session, not a mock that only records the `createSession` argument.
4. (Carry the deferred manuals) c2: no-allowlist profile stays unrestricted; c3: explicit `mcpRole` in the request overrides the profile allowlist.

## Pipeline fix (self-improvement)
`acceptance-contract` must, for any "session excludes X" criterion, require an **end-to-end assertion on the resolved tool set**, not just that config was handed to a mocked `createSession`.

_Source: failure-postmortem of the 2026-06-27 agent-smoke-integration manual smoke._

---
## Consolidated from #735 — Layer 1 (advertise-time MCP scoping)
#735 was the spec for this same problem and code; closed as a duplicate of this issue. Its extra acceptance criteria, folded in here:
- A role-scoped session (e.g. `mcpRole: 'email-assistant'`) connects/advertises **only** that role's servers/tools — an out-of-role tool is literally not callable (advertise-time gate, not just persisted config).
- Verify and **document the actual OpenCode scoping mechanism** — per-directory scoped `.mcp.json` vs a separate opencode instance per role — in a decision file (see `docs/ai/decisions/2026-06-23-c1-mcp-role-sdk-limitation.md`).
- Likely files also include `apps/api_server/src/services/opencode_client_service.ts` and `.mcp-roles/*.mcp.json`.

Part of the agent-security epic **#769**. Layer 2 (dispatch backstop) = #736; content fencing = #737.
trackingInterpretation: Postmortem issue specifically says the previous scope fix was ineffective at runtime and its test was a boundary-only mock. Do not count the cited commit or closed status as behavioral proof; later scope tests/fixes must establish current behavior.

title: Subagent sessions spawned via task.ts bypass MCP allowlist scoping and the Gemini 512-tool cap
body:
## Summary

Agent profiles' `allowedMcpsJson` scope (resolved via `resolveProfileScope()` in
`agent_profile_scope.ts`) and the Gemini 512-function-declaration cap added in
#884 (`capMcpAllowlistForProvider`, see
`docs/ai/decisions/2026-07-02-gemini-tool-cap-choke-point.md`) are only applied
at the two session-creation call sites that go through
`opencode_client_service.ts`: `ws_gateway.ts` (interactive top-level sessions)
and `agent_runner.ts` (scheduled/headless top-level sessions).

A **third call site** creates sessions and is not wired into either mechanism:
`apps/opencode_fork/packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts` — the built-in `task`
tool that spawns a child session whenever a manager profile delegates to a
subagent (`subagent_type: "<profile-id>"`). It calls:

```ts
sessions.create({
  parentID: ctx.sessionID,
  title: params.description + ` (@${next.name} subagent)`,
  permission: [...deriveSubagentSessionPermission(...), ...],
})
```

No `mcpAllowlist` is ever set on the created session. Per the engine's own
contract in `session/mcp_allowlist.ts` (criterion mcp-scope-02-c4: "undefined
allowlist returns all tools (back-compat)"), an unset `mcpAllowlist` means the
child session is **fully unscoped** — every connected MCP server's complete
tool list is exposed to it, regardless of the target profile's own
`allowedMcpsJson` in the `agent_configs` table.

Because this session is created entirely inside the opencode engine process
(not via an HTTP round-trip through `opencode_client_service.ts`), the #884
Gemini cap also never gets a chance to run — so a subagent profile pinned to
`google`/Gemini can blow past the "At most 512 function declarations" limit
even though its own DB scope is correctly narrow.

## Repro

1. Profile `coding-agent` has `allowedMcpsJson: ["rhythm"]` and
   `modelProvider: "google"` / `modelId: "gemini-3.1-flash-lite"`.
2. Run it as a **top-level session** (scheduled task or session picker) →
   scoping + Gemini cap both apply correctly, tool count stays well under 512.
3. Delegate to it via the `task` tool from a manager profile (e.g.
   `workflow-orchestrator` calling `subagent_type: "coding-agent"`) → the
   child session gets `mcpAllowlist: undefined`, exposing every connected MCP
   server (16+ servers, several hundred+ tools) to Gemini, which then fails
   with the proto error "At most 512 function declarations can be specified."

## Expected fix

`task.ts`'s `sessions.create(...)` call needs to resolve and pass an
`mcpAllowlist` for the child session, mirroring what `ws_gateway.ts` /
`agent_runner.ts` already do for top-level sessions — i.e. resolve
`next.name`'s (the `subagent_type`) own profile scope (via
`resolveProfileScope()`/equivalent) and run it through the same
`expandMcpAllowlist()` + `capMcpAllowlistForProvider()` pipeline before
`sessions.create()`, rather than leaving it to inherit the engine's
back-compat "unscoped" default.

Since `task.ts` lives in the vendored `apps/opencode_fork` and doesn't have a
direct import path to api_server's DB-backed `resolveProfileScope()`, this
likely needs either:
- an engine-side callback/host-function the fork can invoke to resolve a named
  agent's scope (mirroring how the fork already gets `Agent.Service` for
  `next = yield* agent.get(params.subagent_type)`), or
- pre-resolving the allowlist for all delegatable profiles at config-sync time
  and attaching it to the `Agent` config the fork already loads, so `task.ts`
  can read `next.mcpAllowlist` directly without a new round-trip.

## Why this matters

Any manager profile whose delegates are pinned to Gemini (directly, or via
`agent_model_resolver.ts`'s `ROUTE_FALLBACKS_BY_AGENT`) will intermittently
fail on delegation with the 512-tool proto error, even though the delegate's
own profile is correctly scoped — the scoping simply never reaches the
session the delegate actually runs in.

## Related

- #884 — original Gemini 512-cap fix (`docs/ai/decisions/2026-07-02-gemini-tool-cap-choke-point.md`)
- mcp-scope-01..06 — the underlying per-session MCP allowlist engine patch
- `docs/ai/decisions/2026-06-25-mcp-scope-02-toolclientnames.md`

Found while diagnosing why the Gemini-routed `coding-agent` profile was
reporting "over 512 tools" despite `allowedMcpsJson` already being scoped to
`["rhythm"]` — traced via `apps/opencode_fork/packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts`.
trackingInterpretation: Historical child-task bypass claim; body explicitly names a missing third creation call site and cites a behavioral contract. Closing issue does not prove later fix, especially absent child-session runtime evidence.

title: Electron agent profiles: redesign settings and actions while preserving the existing page structure
body:
## User clarification
AJ says the Agents tool/profile page structure is good, but the settings/functions UI for each profile is poor. **Preserve the existing profile list and selected-profile editor/inspector structure.** This is a focused redesign of the controls and actions inside each profile, not another page-layout replacement.

## Current evidence
`apps/web/src/components/Profiles.tsx` already has a searchable/selectable profile rail and a profile editor. The editor contains Identity, Delegation, Availability, Provider & model, Capabilities, and Core permission rules. The live capabilities UI renders lists of MCP tool and skill checkboxes, while live core permissions are exposed as a raw JSON textarea. These are concrete starting points for the control-design pass; this report does not establish that their backend behavior is broken.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Retain the existing profile-list/inspector arrangement and selection flow. Focus changes on each profile's settings, functions, and action presentation.
- [ ] Make the selected profile easy to understand at a glance: clear identity/status, meaningful section hierarchy, aligned labels/controls, readable descriptions, consistent spacing, and restrained visual treatment.
- [ ] Give identity/instructions, provider/model/account, delegation, availability/defaults, capabilities, and permissions coherent groups with plain-language explanations where needed. Frequently used controls should be easy to find; advanced details should remain discoverable without overwhelming the editor.
- [ ] Make long MCP/tool and skill lists manageable through clear grouping, selection summaries, and filtering or disclosure as appropriate. Preserve complete access to individual choices and communicate inherited/explicit selections accurately.
- [ ] Provide understandable controls for common permission choices rather than requiring raw JSON for ordinary edits. Preserve full existing policy semantics, including inheritance, per-tool patterns, and advanced/unknown entries; retain an explicit advanced editing path where necessary and never silently flatten or discard policy data.
- [ ] Place profile-level actions consistently, with clear distinction between normal editing, immediate actions, and destructive actions. Preserve all existing profile functions and their authorization/confirmation requirements.
- [ ] Make save/cancel, unsaved changes, validation, saving, success, and failure states unambiguous. Switching profiles must not silently discard edits or apply them to the wrong profile.
- [ ] Preserve actual live behavior and persistence for each setting. Fixture-only controls must not be presented as working live functionality.
- [ ] Ensure keyboard navigation, focus, labels, read-only states, long content, and smaller windows remain usable; sticky actions must not cover fields.

## Likely files
- `apps/web/src/components/Profiles.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/styles.css`
- `apps/web/src/gateway/sessions.ts` and existing profile store wiring only if required to support the redesigned controls
- `apps/web/tests/inspector-profiles.spec.ts`
- `apps/web/tests/post-m1-phase-2-profiles.redspec.ts`
- `apps/web/tests/post-m1-phase-2-profile-security.redspec.ts`
- `apps/web/tests/post-m1-phase-5-permissions.redspec.ts`

## Required evaluation
Capture before/after views of the same profile in the actual Electron/live UI. Verify representative profile editing, model/account selection, delegation, large capability catalogs, permissions, save/cancel, failure, and profile-switching flows. Include policy round-trip checks proving structured edits preserve advanced rules and defaults. Use isolated profiles/data for persistence tests and clearly separate rendered fixture evidence from live verification. Obtain a manual visual review of the revised inspector before calling the design accepted.

## Dependencies / related work
#1513 owns the shared Agent Tools visual pattern; the existing Profiles structure is already acceptable and should be retained. #1514 owns missing controls on the separate Agent Settings page. This issue owns the usability and visual quality of the per-profile editor. Coordinate readability with #1509.

## Safety / out of scope
Issue filing only at this stage. No implementation or changes to live profiles. Preserve permission defaults, capability scoping, approval rules, and account bindings; a visual redesign must not broaden agent access. No backend schema redesign, automatic agent runs, deployment, or unrelated page restructuring.
trackingInterpretation: Design acceptance is all unchecked at filing; issue says backend was not established broken. Treat as UX/control redesign intent, not evidence of implemented controls or backend defect.

title: [COL-01] Pin upstream Colony source and emit a sealed embedded artifact
body:
## Goal

Pin an exact upstream Bot Crossing revision and have that upstream project emit a sealed, integrity-verified embedded artifact that Rhythm can consume. Rhythm holds a pinned commit constant and nothing else — no vendored source tree.

Parent: #1525

Plan: [Colony in Rhythm Electron](https://github.com/ajhochy/Rhythm/blob/codex/colony-integration-plan/docs/ai/plans/2026-09-18-electron-colony.md)

Milestone: Colony M1 — Foundation and local runtime

## Dependencies

None within this plan.

## Approach note (revised 2026-09-21)

This follows the Hermes Desktop precedent (`6ed3ba03`; `apps/electron/src/hermes-desktop-config.mjs`, `src/hermes-desktop-artifact.mjs`). The earlier draft of this issue vendored a source copy into `apps/colony/` with `UPSTREAM.json` and import tooling. That is replaced: upstream stays upstream, and the integration surface is a build artifact, not a codebase. It removes the merge/drift burden and the duplicate test suite, and it is what made the Hermes integration go smoothly.

## Likely files

- Bot Crossing (upstream): `apps/desktop`-equivalent `build:rhythm-embedded` script and its own test
- Bot Crossing (upstream): notice/licence staging into the artifact output
- Rhythm: new `apps/electron/src/colony-desktop-config.mjs` exporting `PINNED_COLONY_SOURCE_COMMIT`
- Rhythm: `docs/ai/plans/2026-09-18-electron-colony.md` pinned build inputs

## Requirements

- Review the exact Bot fork revision and its draft stack before pinning; candidate `36d2c29989f567de0ac4d30a957610163cfc4d86` includes ajhochy/bot-crossing#4. Do not track a moving branch.
- Add `build:rhythm-embedded` upstream. It emits `build/rhythm-embedded/` containing the renderer entry, the scanner host entry, the preload entry, all required third-party notices, and `manifest.json`.
- `manifest.json` schema: `schemaVersion` (1), `product` (`colony`), `sourceCommit` (40-hex), `electronMajor`, `dirty`/`sourceDirty` booleans, `files` mapping the required entry points (`renderer`, `host`, `preload`) to artifact-relative paths, and `integrity` mapping **every** file in the tree to a `sha256-<base64>` SRI digest.
- The builder refuses to emit a clean manifest from a dirty working tree, and records the source revision it actually built. It writes no symlinks and no absolute paths.
- Rhythm stores only `PINNED_COLONY_SOURCE_COMMIT`. There is no `apps/colony/` source tree, no import script, no submodule and no sibling-checkout requirement.
- Record the pinned build inputs in the plan: source revision, Electron major, exact Node patch (with `node:sqlite` support) and minimum macOS version. The Electron major is decided here, not discovered downstream — Hermes found Electron 33 shipped Node 20 without global WebSocket and had to move Rhythm to 40.10.2.
- Exclude `data/*.json`, local native-openers configuration, `.env`, transcripts, private screenshots, user audio and development credentials from the artifact.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **COL-01-AC1:** A clean upstream checkout at the pinned revision runs `build:rhythm-embedded` and emits an artifact whose `manifest.json` names that exact revision, the agreed `electronMajor`, and the three required entry points; no adjacent Rhythm checkout is needed.
- [ ] **COL-01-AC2:** Running the builder twice on the same pinned inputs produces identical `integrity` digests, or the nondeterministic fields are explicitly documented and excluded from the seal.
- [ ] **COL-01-AC3:** Building from a dirty working tree either fails or sets `dirty: true`; every file in the emitted tree appears in `integrity`, and the tree contains no symlink, no absolute path and no excluded developer/user data.
- [ ] **COL-01-AC4:** The artifact contains the applicable MIT/CC0/Apache-2.0 notices for the shipped inventory, covered by `integrity` so they cannot drift from the code; a missing or unlicensed asset fails the build. Asset size baseline is recorded for later package comparison.
- [ ] **COL-01-AC5:** The upstream adapter/state test suite still passes at the pinned revision, preserving task IDs, parent/worker relationships, repository/checkout grouping and local archive/viewed state; before/after source-store evidence shows no harness writes.

## Required tests / evaluation

- Upstream: a builder test asserting manifest shape, full integrity coverage, dirty-tree refusal and the excluded-path denylist (Hermes analogue: `build-embedded-artifact.test.mjs`).
- Upstream: run the existing adapter/state suite and production build at the pinned revision; retain the synthetic regression coverage rather than replacing it with build-path assertions.
- Record the artifact file count, asset size baseline and hash input manifest for later package comparison.

## Safety and scope

All-user opt-in; macOS Apple Silicon and Intel. Discovery is read-only; Colony writes only its own profile-scoped preferences/cache. No cloud upload of harness data, provider-secret changes, automatic agent turns, source deletions, or takeover/restart of live API/engine services. Use the canonical isolated sandbox for any needed backend smoke. New-session/terminal-resume actions and Flutter retirement are outside this plan. Work on a feature branch, capture required evidence and open a draft PR; human merge/release remains separate.
trackingInterpretation: Open Colony M1 artifact pin/seal work; source plan explicitly revised away from vendored source. Not evidence Colony shipped.

title: [COL-02] Verify the Colony artifact and add the isolated embedded bridge
body:
## Goal

Verify the sealed Colony artifact before Rhythm's privileged process imports it, then expose the Colony data operations and 3D scene through explicit embedded contracts — without a public local HTTP server, broad native privileges, or any fallback loading path.

Parent: #1525

Plan: [Colony in Rhythm Electron](https://github.com/ajhochy/Rhythm/blob/codex/colony-integration-plan/docs/ai/plans/2026-09-18-electron-colony.md)

Milestone: Colony M1 — Foundation and local runtime

## Dependencies

#1526

## Approach note (revised 2026-09-21)

Adds the artifact resolver, modelled on `apps/electron/src/hermes-desktop-artifact.mjs`. The earlier draft had no integrity/refusal contract at all — only "a packaged app with missing resources must fail clearly." Refusing an unprovable artifact with no fallback is the specific reason the Hermes integration never produced a "works in dev, broken installed" build.

## Likely files

- Proposed `apps/electron/src/colony-desktop-artifact.mjs` (resolver + re-seal helper)
- Proposed `apps/electron/test/colony-desktop-artifact.test.mjs`
- Proposed `apps/electron/src/colony-protocol.mjs` and `colony-policy.mjs`
- `apps/electron/src/main.mjs`, `preload.cjs`; `apps/web/index.html`
- Upstream embedded service/worker entry and scene adapter (`src/game/api.js` seam)
- Proposed `apps/shared/colony-contract.*` and contract tests

## Requirements

**Artifact verification.** `resolveColonyArtifact({ artifactRoot, expectedElectronMajor, expectedSourceCommit, allowDirty })` validates before any import and throws an actionable error on each of:

- missing artifact root, or a missing/unreadable/non-object `manifest.json`
- `schemaVersion` or `product` mismatch
- `sourceCommit` that is not 40-hex, or does not equal `PINNED_COLONY_SOURCE_COMMIT`
- `electronMajor` not equal to the running Electron major
- `dirty` or `sourceDirty` true (unless `allowDirty` is explicitly set), or either present but non-boolean
- empty `integrity`, a duplicate entry, a malformed SRI value, or any digest mismatch
- any file present in the tree but absent from `integrity`
- any symlink, any non-regular entry, any absolute manifest path, or any path escaping the artifact root
- a missing or unverified `renderer`, `host` or `preload` entry

There is **no** development-mode loading path, **no** `BOT_CROSSING_DATA` PATH lookup and **no** degraded standalone fallback. The single seam is `RHYTHM_COLONY_ARTIFACT_DIR`, which must point at a real built artifact passing identical validation; `allowDirty` is the only relaxation and is never set in packaging or CI.

Also provide `refreshColonyArtifactIntegrity({ artifactRoot })` for the post-codesign re-seal used by COL-09.

**Embedded contracts.** Extract shared service operations from the upstream API; keep the standalone HTTP adapter working upstream. Define versioned DTOs and scene intents for selection, filters, camera, viewport, theme and visibility. Serve only the verified artifact's renderer entry on a fixed separate origin; use a document-bound MessageChannel and narrow preload entry points, validating host/frame identity, current document generation, method and payload at each privileged boundary. Keep Node integration off and sandbox/context isolation/web security on; never enable `bypassCSP`; never send auth/provider credentials to the scene. Bound control requests to 64 KiB, pages/chunks to 1 MiB and inventory pages to 250 records; large local state uses bounded chunks, a 32 MiB aggregate limit and one validated atomic commit. No silent truncation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **COL-02-AC1:** Each refusal case above is covered by a direct unit test and produces a distinct actionable error with zero import, zero native action and zero state write. Corrupting one byte of one artifact file fails the load.
- [ ] **COL-02-AC2:** With `RHYTHM_COLONY_ARTIFACT_DIR` unset or pointing at a missing, dirty, wrong-commit or wrong-`electronMajor` artifact, the Colony tab reports why and stops; no alternative source is loaded and no partial UI is shown.
- [ ] **COL-02-AC3:** In real pinned Electron, artifact-served JS/GLB assets load and a synthetic scan plus state round-trip works through private child IPC; no Colony TCP listener is created and upstream standalone HTTP behavior still passes.
- [ ] **COL-02-AC4:** A sibling/foreign frame, stale/reloaded document, unknown method, malformed/oversize message and unsupported protocol version each produce zero native actions and zero state writes.
- [ ] **COL-02-AC5:** The scene cannot access Rhythm bearer tokens, parent DOM, arbitrary URLs, filesystem APIs or process APIs; leaving/disabling the feature revokes the previous channel.
- [ ] **COL-02-AC6:** A 15,000-record snapshot is paged with stable generation/cursors and cancellation; a large archive beyond 64 KiB round-trips unchanged, while an interrupted state transfer commits nothing.

## Required tests / evaluation

- A dedicated resolver test file exercising every refusal rule with fixture artifacts, kept separate from the live/native suite.
- Service parity tests over shared HTTP/embedded fixtures, including archive conflicts and cancellation.
- Real Electron protocol/hostile-frame/message-lifetime tests on the pinned runtime; a plain browser test is not sufficient.
- Falsify one sender-validation check, one integrity check and one chunk/atomic-commit guard to show the tests catch the failure.

## Safety and scope

All-user opt-in; macOS Apple Silicon and Intel. Discovery is read-only; Colony writes only its own profile-scoped preferences/cache. No cloud upload of harness data, provider-secret changes, automatic agent turns, source deletions, or takeover/restart of live API/engine services. Use the canonical isolated sandbox for any needed backend smoke. New-session/terminal-resume actions and Flutter retirement are outside this plan. Work on a feature branch, capture required evidence and open a draft PR; human merge/release remains separate.
trackingInterpretation: Open Colony bridge requirement rejects unverified artifacts and fallback loading; acceptance still outstanding by issue state.

title: [COL-04] Design the Rhythm-native Colony workspace and menu system
body:
## Goal

Produce a concrete UI and menu design that makes Colony feel native to Rhythm Electron while retaining the 3D world and multi-harness clarity.

Parent: #1525

Plan: [Colony in Rhythm Electron](https://github.com/ajhochy/Rhythm/blob/codex/colony-integration-plan/docs/ai/plans/2026-09-18-electron-colony.md)

Milestone: Colony M2 — Rhythm-native UI and menus

## Dependencies

None within this plan.

## Likely files

- docs/ai/plans/2026-09-18-electron-colony.md design brief
- Proposed docs/design/colony/ annotated comps and action inventory
- Visual references: apps/web/src/styles.css, components/Shell.tsx, Tasks and Agents workspaces
- Reference: adopted Colony HUD, task card, filters and scene/view controls

## Requirements

- Use Rhythm Tasks/Agents typography, tokens, icons, panel density, buttons, menus and resize/focus behavior as the visual authority. Preserve the world/characters; remove duplicate global chrome in embedded mode.
- Define one Colony destination; a resizable repository/task rail, central scene and optional inspector; compact search/filters/status; and a native-style View menu for camera/world/sound/quality controls.
- Map every current action to a final location, explicit deferment or removal. Use Open in Rhythm/Open in Codex, Show parent task and Archive from Colony/Restore to Colony. Do not expose unqualified new-session/terminal-resume actions.

title: [COL-09] Stage the sealed Colony artifact in the Mac package
body:
## Goal

Stage the sealed, verified Colony artifact into the Mac package so the installed Rhythm app contains the renderer, scanner, assets and notices without any development tooling — and so the UI in M2 develops against the exact payload that ships.

Parent: #1525

Plan: [Colony in Rhythm Electron](https://github.com/ajhochy/Rhythm/blob/codex/colony-integration-plan/docs/ai/plans/2026-09-18-electron-colony.md)

Milestone: Colony M3 — Packaged Apple Silicon and Intel builds

## Dependencies

#1527, #1528

## Approach note (revised 2026-09-21)

**Reordered.** This previously depended on #1532 and #1533, placing packaging behind the entire UI and forcing COL-05 to develop against a fixture contract. Hermes landed the resolver, the packager staging, the re-seal step and the CI producer in the same foundational change as the view, so the interface and the shipped package never disagreed about what loads. This issue now depends only on M1 and runs in parallel with M2; #1530 depends on it.

## Likely files

- `apps/electron/scripts/package-mac.mjs` (new `stageColonyArtifact`, re-seal call)
- `apps/electron/src/colony-desktop-artifact.mjs`, `colony-desktop-config.mjs` (copied into the packaged app)
- `apps/electron/src/colony-service.mjs` and protocol resource lookup
- Proposed `apps/electron/test/colony-package.test.mjs`

## Requirements

- `stageColonyArtifact({ resources, artifactRoot = process.env.RHYTHM_COLONY_ARTIFACT_DIR })` throws when the variable is unset. Packaging must never assemble from an absent or unverified payload.
- Validate the source artifact against `PINNED_COLONY_SOURCE_COMMIT` and the runtime Electron major with `allowDirty: false`, copy it into immutable resources with `verbatimSymlinks`, then **re-validate at the destination**.
- Sign nested executables first; then call `refreshColonyArtifactIntegrity` on the staged artifact; then re-validate; then re-apply **only** the outer signature. `codesign` rewrites nested binaries, so sealing before signing guarantees a first-launch digest mismatch.
- Copy the resolver and config modules into the packaged app alongside the service, so the installed app performs the same validation the packager did.
- Extend the existing bundled Node path. Pin a supported exact Node patch and verify `node:sqlite`, architecture and worker startup before accepting a payload.
- Build with neutral environment inputs, stage only production resources, and store writable state in userData only. The app must start offline: no npm install, art download, Homebrew lookup or sibling checkout at runtime.
- Test a clean Mac with developer tools unavailable and no system Node; preserve task discovery with honest metadata degradation and no installation prompt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **COL-09-AC1:** The packaged app starts Colony against synthetic stores with the repository checkout unavailable and PATH containing no Node/npm; all assets and scanner capabilities load from the staged artifact.
- [ ] **COL-09-AC2:** Packaging with `RHYTHM_COLONY_ARTIFACT_DIR` unset, or pointing at a dirty/wrong-commit/corrupt artifact, fails the build with an actionable message; no development-path fallback masks it.
- [ ] **COL-09-AC3:** Removing or corrupting one staged artifact file after packaging produces a clear unavailable state at first launch rather than a partial or silently degraded Colony tab.
- [ ] **COL-09-AC4:** A repeat package build from identical pinned inputs produces matching app manifests; the re-seal step is the only source of post-signing manifest change, and the outer signature verifies strictly after it.
- [ ] **COL-09-AC5:** A payload inventory identifies source revision, exact Node/architecture and dependency/asset hashes; scans find no user data, fixture identities/tokens, inherited Vite secrets or developer-specific paths.
- [ ] **COL-09-AC6:** Packaging leaves local preferences untouched and records archive/installed-size deltas; offline enablement works with empty sources and populated fixtures.

## Required tests / evaluation

- Use the actual unsigned .app on the host architecture for no-checkout/no-PATH/offline/missing-resource/corrupted-file cases.
- A package test covering the unset-variable refusal, the destination re-validation and the seal/sign ordering.
- Run scanner/state tests with the exact packaged Node, including a real read-only SQLite fixture.
- Verify the manifest and all source/art/icon notices against the staged payload.

## Safety and scope

All-user opt-in; macOS Apple Silicon and Intel. Discovery is read-only; Colony writes only its own profile-scoped preferences/cache. No cloud upload of harness data, provider-secret changes, automatic agent turns, source deletions, or takeover/restart of live API/engine services. title: Electron Accounts: re-authorize expired accounts and connect OpenAI/Google/OpenCode/OpenRouter
body:
## Root cause

Two separate gaps, both in `apps/web` — the server needed no change.

**1. No way to re-log in.** The account rows in `AgentSettingsTool.tsx` rendered only
"Make default" and "Remove". An account the refresh loop marked `needs_relogin` (the
user's *default* account, `personal`) could only be recovered by deleting and recreating
it, and `connectedAccounts` silently excluded it without flagging it anywhere.

The backend was never the problem. Verified against the running instance on :4001:

```
POST /opencode/auth/accounts/login-start {"accountId":"personal","label":"Personal"} -> 200 {authorizeUrl:...}
GET  /opencode/auth/accounts  (unchanged: personal still present, still defaultAccountId)
```

`AnthropicAccountsStore.upsertAccount` replaces by id and leaves `defaultAccountId`
untouched, so re-authorizing in place is exactly the existing login-start/login-complete
pair with an id the store already knows.

**2. Provider auth never made it into the Electron build.** `GET /opencode/auth`,
`/:provider/authorize`, `/:provider/callback` and `POST /:provider` all exist and are
used by the Flutter client; the React page simply had no UI for them.

## Shape of the diff

- **`AgentSettingsTool.tsx`**
  - `beginAccountLogin(accountId, label)` extracted from the form handler; the "Authorize"
    form now calls it, and each `needs_relogin` row gets a **Re-authorize** button that
    calls it with that account's own id/label. A "Needs re-authorization" badge and a
    warning border make the stale account visible, and the section subtitle counts them.
  - New **Model providers** block, ported from
    `apps/desktop_flutter/lib/features/settings/widgets/ai_account_section.dart` — same
    endpoints, same method indexes:
    | Provider | Flow |
    |---|---|
    | OpenAI / Codex | OAuth `method=1` (paste-back — the callback URL or code) |
    | Google / Gemini | OAuth `method=0`; the engine plugin's own local listener finishes the exchange, so the UI re-reads `GET /opencode/auth` instead of posting a code |
    | OpenCode | API key → `POST /opencode/auth/opencode` |
    | OpenRouter | API key → `POST /opencode/auth/openrouter` |
- **`gateway/sessions.ts`** — four optional methods (`authProviders`, `authorizeProvider`,
  `completeProviderAuth`, `saveProviderApiKey`) next to the existing accounts methods. No
  new gateway domain, no `index.ts` wiring.
- **`AgentSettingsTool.css`** — account rows were inheriting the 34px avatar column meant
  for profile rows; they now use `1fr auto`. Plus the stale-account warning border.
- **Tests** — two specs in the existing live-boundary style, and
  `tests/agent-settings-accounts-playwright.config.ts`, because the
  "Agent Settings live persistence" block needed a live-gateway dev server that no config
  targeted, so those specs had never actually executed.

No `apps/api_server` change was required.

## Evidence

```
npm run typecheck                                   pass
npm run build                                       pass
RHYTHM_LIVE_E2E=1 npx playwright test \
  --config tests/agent-settings-accounts-playwright.config.ts   4 passed
```

The two new specs assert the behaviours that were missing: the expired **default** account
is re-authorized in place (default retained, sibling account untouched, exactly
`start:personal` + `complete:personal` on the wire), and OpenAI goes out on `method=1`
while Google goes out on `method=0`.

## What to click to verify

Agent settings → **Accounts**:

1. `Personal` shows **Needs re-authorization** with a warning border, and the section
   subtitle reads `1 need re-authorization`.
2. Click **Re-authorize** on that row → "Authorizing Personal" appears with the Anthropic
   link. Sign in, paste the code, **Save account** → the badge clears and the row is still
   **Default**. Nothing was deleted.
3. Scroll to **Model providers**: **Connect** on OpenAI / Codex, sign in, paste the
   `http://localhost:1455/auth/callback?code=…` URL back, **Finish connecting**.
4. **Connect** on Google / Gemini, finish in the browser, then
   **I finished sign-in — check connection**.
5. Paste OpenCode and OpenRouter keys into their rows and **Save key**.

Each row flips to **Connected** off the live `GET /opencode/auth` list, not off local state.

## Note for the models/fallback workstream

`GET /agents/models` returning `[]` is **not** caused by the expired default account — the
route requires `?agentId=`. With it, `claude-code`, `codex` and `opencode` all return
populated lists, and `/agents/models/catalog` reports `authorized: true` for anthropic on
this machine right now.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
trackingInterpretation: Merged PR reports reauthorization and provider auth work with live :4001 HTTP observations, but merge is not installed Electron/product proof; retain its explicit app boundary.

title: Electron Agent Settings: MCP failed/needs_auth servers look identical to connected ones, and their errors are styled as muted text
body:
## Problem In the **live** MCP servers section (`apps/web/src/components/tools/AgentSettingsTool.tsx:452`), a broken server is visually identical to a healthy one, and its error message is styled as the least prominent text on the card. Measured on the running desktop app (26 configured servers, 21 connected): | server | status | rendered badge colour | |---|---|---| | `engraph`, `gitnexus`, `rhythm`, … (21) | `connected` | `rgb(191, 198, 195)` | | `canva`, `notion` | `needs_auth` | `rgb(191, 198, 195)` | | `mailchimp`, `ableton-mcp`, `propresenter` | `failed` | `rgb(191, 198, 195)` | Three root causes: 1. **The badge has no state variants.** The status renders as a bare `.kind-badge` (`styles.css:638`), which is a fixed neutral pill. `styles.css:640` only colours `.state-badge.failed` and `.risk-badge.medium` — nothing colours a `.kind-badge`. 2. **The error message is explicitly muted.** `AgentSettingsTool.css:22–29` sets `.agent-settings-mcp-list p { color: var(--muted) }`, and the server error is rendered as `

` inside that list. So `MCP error -32000: Connection closed` is painted in the dimmest colour on the card — dimmer than the server name, dimmer than the source/tool-count line. 3. **Raw server-side status strings are shown verbatim.** `needs_auth` reaches the badge unchanged; `text-transform: capitalize` renders it as `Needs_auth`. `.kind-badge` is also `font-size: 8px`. ## What the user sees Scrolling 26 near-identical cards with no way to tell which five are broken. The `mailchimp` card reads: ``` mailchimp [ Failed ] curated · 0 tools MCP error -32000: Connection closed <- muted, smallest text on the card Credentials required <- also muted MAILCHIMP_API_KEY [ ] [ Save credentials ] [ Connect ] Remove <- Connect is disabled at 0.52 opacity, looks live ``` The only honest signal that something is wrong is the word "Failed" in an 8px grey pill in the corner. ## Why it matters Accounts — rebuilt in `05ca632c` and the agreed quality bar — already solves exactly this: `AgentSettingsTool.css:162–169` gives a stale account `border-color: var(--warning)` on the card **and** recolours its badge, so an account needing re-authorization is visible without reading. MCP needs the same treatment. Until it does, a broken tool connection is silently invisible, and the agent quietly loses those tools. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `connected`, `needs_auth` and `failed` are visually distinct at a glance — card border and badge colour, matching the `.needs-relogin` treatment Accounts uses for stale accounts. - [ ] A server's error message is **not** muted. It reads as an error (error colour / icon), and it is not the least prominent text in its own card. - [ ] Status strings are mapped to human labels ("Connected", "Needs authorization", "Failed"), never raw snake_case from the API. - [ ] The status badge meets the WCAG AA contrast minimum against the card background at its rendered size; if 8px cannot, raise the size. - [ ] Do not encode status by colour alone — keep the text label alongside the colour. - [ ] Rendered regression coverage with at least one `connected`, one `needs_auth` and one `failed` server asserting distinct rendered classes/colours. ## Likely files - `apps/web/src/components/tools/AgentSettingsTool.tsx:452` (the MCP card) - `apps/web/src/components/tools/AgentSettingsTool.css:22–29` (the `p` muting rule), `:162–169` (the Accounts pattern to copy) - `apps/web/src/styles.css:638–640` (`.kind-badge` / `.state-badge` variants) ## Out of scope No change to MCP connect/disconnect behaviour or to the gateway's status values. Presentation only. Fixing the three servers that are actually failing is a separate matter.
trackingInterpretation: Open issue asserts live broken/needs_auth states are visually indistinguishable and errors muted; this is a precise user-visible gap, not contradictory to backend connection support.

Accounts — rebuilt in `05ca632c`, the agreed quality bar — uses the **opposite** order at lines 414–436: the existing account records render first, then the "Authorize Anthropic account" form below them. MCP is the only section that inverts it.

## What the user sees

Opening MCP servers, the first screen is an empty three-field form. Every one of the 26 configured servers is below the fold. There is no search, no filter, no grouping, and the list is in API order, so the five servers that need attention (`canva`, `notion` → `needs_auth`; `mailchimp`, `ableton-mcp`, `propresenter` → `failed`) are scattered among 21 healthy ones and can only be found by scrolling the whole list.

Each card is roughly 80px tall with a `Disconnect` / `Remove` pair, so the section is ~2,000px of near-identical rows.

Two further consequences, both observed live:

- Because the whole page scrolls (the inspector pane is not independently scrolled at this size), the **section list rail scrolls off the top** while you page through servers — you lose the Agent Settings navigation entirely partway down.
- `ListInspector` already supports `searchable` / `groups` (`ListInspector.tsx:40–58`), but the MCP server list is a plain `<div>` inside the inspector, so none of that is available to it.

## Why it matters

The section's job is "see which tool connections are healthy and fix the ones that aren't". The current layout optimises for the rarest action (adding a server) and makes the common one (finding the broken server) a scroll hunt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The list of configured servers renders **above** the add form, matching the Accounts order.
- [ ] Adding a server does not occupy the top of the section by default — put it behind a disclosure or a secondary "Add server" action that reveals the form.
- [ ] Servers needing attention (`failed`, `needs_auth`) are reachable without scrolling the full list: either sorted to the top, grouped by status, or filterable.
- [ ] The list is searchable by server name when there are more than ~10 servers.
- [ ] The section-list rail stays reachable while scrolling a long inspector (sticky rail, or scroll the inspector pane rather than the page).
- [ ] Verified at 1440px and at a narrow window with the real 26-server workspace, not a two-item fixture.

## Likely files

- `apps/web/src/components/tools/AgentSettingsTool.tsx:438–453`
- `apps/web/src/components/tools/AgentSettingsTool.css:61–97`
- `apps/web/src/components/ListInspector.css:1–33, 64` (rail/detail scroll containment)

## Out of scope

No change to the MCP add/connect/remove API calls. Layout and ordering only. Status colouring is tracked separately.
trackingInterpretation: Open issue documents MCP form-first ordering and no search/filter/grouping across 26 servers; do not claim broken-server discoverability is covered by connection CRUD.

title: Timestamps render as raw UTC ISO strings across the Electron renderer; no shared formatter
body:
## What the user sees

Message timestamps in the Electron agent transcript render as the raw ISO string:

```
2026-09-21T20:01:40.000Z
```

Two problems, and the second is worse than the first:

1. It is machine output shown to a human — punctuation, milliseconds, and a `Z` suffix.
2. **It is UTC, not local.** The screenshot above was taken at **1:01 PM Pacific**. A user reading this sees "20:01" and has to subtract seven hours in their head to know when their own message was sent.

This is a regression of #1010 ("Show all timestamps in Pacific time, 12-hour AM/PM — agents UI + everywhere"), which was closed against the Flutter client. The Electron renderer never received the equivalent treatment.

## Root cause

`apps/web/src/components/Transcript.tsx:341` interpolates the ISO string directly into the element body:

```tsx
<time dateTime={message.createdAt}>{message.createdAt}</time>
```

`dateTime` is correct — that attribute *should* carry the machine-readable ISO value. The element's text content should carry a human-readable local rendering, and instead repeats the raw string.

## Inventory — this is not one site

Raw ISO rendered directly:

| File | Line | Field |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/components/Transcript.tsx` | 341 | `message.createdAt` (the screenshot) |
| `apps/web/src/components/ToolWorkspace.tsx` | 612 | `run.startedAt` |
| `apps/web/src/components/ToolWorkspace.tsx` | 1199, 1210 | `signal.receivedAt \|\| signal.createdAt` |
| `apps/web/src/pages/messages/live.tsx` | 268 | `message.createdAt` |
| `apps/web/src/pages/messages/index.tsx` | 371 | `message.createdAt` |
| `apps/web/src/pages/mobile-access/index.tsx` | 289 | `device.createdAt` |

**There is no shared date formatter in `apps/web`.** Every surface that does format invents its own:

- `pages/messages/live.tsx:39` — `toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit' })`
- `pages/planner/index.tsx:32-34` — three `Intl.DateTimeFormat` instances, all pinned `timeZone: 'UTC'`
- `pages/dashboard/index.tsx:676` — inline `toLocaleDateString`
- `pages/dashboard/LiveArtifactsShell.tsx:23` — a local `formatDate()`

So the same app renders the same instant in at least four different shapes, some local and some UTC.

## Separate defect found in the same sweep

`apps/web/src/components/Inspector.tsx:48` **hard-codes the date** and slices characters out of the ISO string for the time:

```tsx
<dt>Created</dt><dd>Aug 12 · {selected.createdAt.slice(11, 16)}</dd>
<dt>Updated</dt><dd>Aug 12 · {selected.updatedAt.slice(11, 16)}</dd>
```

Every session reports "Aug 12" regardless of when it was created, and `.slice(11, 16)` yields the UTC clock time, not local. This file reads from `useFixtures()`, so **confirm whether this path renders in the live app before fixing** — if it is fixture-only the severity drops, but the hard-coded literal should go either way.

## Proposed fix

One shared helper in `apps/web/src`, used by every site above and by the four ad-hoc formatters. Do not add a date library — `Intl.DateTimeFormat` covers this.

It should render in the **viewer's local timezone** (omit `timeZone` rather than pinning `'UTC'`), 12-hour with AM/PM per #1010, and relative for recent values ("2m ago", "Yesterday 4:12 PM") where a transcript benefits from it. Keep the machine-readable ISO in `dateTime` attributes for accessibility and copy-paste.

Note the planner's deliberate `timeZone: 'UTC'` pins — determine whether those are intentional (all-day/date-only values, where local conversion would shift the day) before changing them. Date-only values genuinely should not be localized; instants should.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A single shared timestamp formatter exists in `apps/web` and is used by all six raw-ISO sites listed above.
- [ ] The four existing ad-hoc formatters are replaced by it, or a documented reason is given for each that is not.
- [ ] No raw ISO string is rendered as visible text anywhere in `apps/web`; a lint rule or test guards this.
- [ ] Rendered times are in the viewer's local timezone and 12-hour AM/PM. A message sent at 1:01 PM Pacific displays as 1:01 PM, not 20:01.
- [ ] `<time>` elements retain the ISO value in `dateTime`.
- [ ] The hard-coded `Aug 12` in `Inspector.tsx:48` is gone, and the issue states whether that path is live or fixture-only.
- [ ] The planner's UTC pins are either kept with a comment explaining why, or converted.
trackingInterpretation: Open issue reports Electron raw ISO timestamp rendering and says #1010 only closed Flutter path; this contradicts any broad claim that timestamp formatting is already complete across clients.

title: OpenAI usage budget is reachable: Codex plan windows come from GET /backend-api/wham/usage, not the platform API
body:
## Summary

`GET /agents/usage-budget` reports every provider's remaining quota except OpenAI, which is hard-coded to `unavailable`:

```ts
// apps/api_server/src/services/usage_budget_service.ts:255-266
reason: 'No usage API for the ChatGPT-plan token (standard API returns 401; Codex usage backend is undocumented).'
```

**The reason string is wrong on its second clause.** The Codex usage backend is undocumented in the sense that OpenAI publishes no reference page for it — but it is fully readable from the open-source Codex CLI, it is a plain authenticated `GET` that costs zero tokens, and Rhythm already holds the credential it needs. **Yes, there is a way.**

This issue is research + a proposed mechanism only. No product code was changed.

Related: #1566 (the usage-panel parity issue, which currently expects OpenAI to render as `unavailable` — that expectation should be revised if this lands).

---

## 1. How Anthropic's budget is actually obtained (the working reference)

Not a usage API. A **response-header harvest off a deliberately minimal live API call**.

`apps/api_server/src/services/usage_budget_service.ts:172-220` — `probeAnthropicAccount()`:

- `POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`, `max_tokens: 1`, model `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, body `"hi"`.
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <OAuth access token>`, `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20`.
- Reads from the **response headers**, never the body:
  - `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-5h-utilization` / `-5h-reset` / `-5h-status`
  - `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-7d-utilization` / `-7d-reset` / `-7d-status`
- `remainingFraction = 1 - utilization`; reset epoch → ISO.
- Per-account (#907) via `anthropicAccountsService`; cached 60s (`CACHE_TTL_MS`) specifically so the probe — which does consume one request against the window — runs at most ~once/minute.

So the template is: *the provider already tells you your remaining quota on traffic you're making anyway; you just have to read it.* Gemini (`cloudcode-pa…:retrieveUserQuota`) and OpenRouter (`GET /api/v1/key`) are the polled-endpoint variants.

For OpenAI, **both** variants exist — and the polled one is strictly better, because it is free.

---

## 2. Line 1 — Response headers: CONFIRMED, they exist, and Rhythm throws them away

The ChatGPT-Codex backend emits an `x-codex-*` header family on every Codex Responses response. Parser, upstream, verbatim:

`openai/codex` → `codex-rs/codex-api/src/rate_limits.rs`, `parse_rate_limit_for_limit()`:

```rust
let prefix = format!("x-{normalized_limit}");       // "x-codex" by default
let primary = parse_rate_limit_window(
    headers,
    &format!("{prefix}-primary-used-percent"),
    &format!("{prefix}-primary-window-minutes"),
    &format!("{prefix}-primary-reset-at"),
);
let secondary = parse_rate_limit_window(
    headers,
    &format!("{prefix}-secondary-used-percent"),
    &format!("{prefix}-secondary-window-minutes"),
    &format!("{prefix}-secondary-reset-at"),
);
```

Plus, in the same file:

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `x-codex-primary-used-percent` / `-primary-window-minutes` / `-primary-reset-at` | 5h window (`window_minutes: 300`) |
| `x-codex-secondary-used-percent` / `-secondary-window-minutes` / `-secondary-reset-at` | weekly window (`10080`) |
| `x-codex-limit-name`, `x-codex-active-limit` | which metered limit these describe |
| `x-codex-credits-has-credits` / `-credits-unlimited` / `-credits-balance` | `parse_credits_snapshot()` |
| `x-codex-rate-limit-reached-type` | `parse_rate_limit_reached_type()` |
| `x-codex-promo-message` | `parse_promo_message()` |

Independently confirmed against the binary actually installed on this machine — `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/codex/0.153.4/bin/codex` (codex-cli 0.153.4) — where `strings` yields the literals `-primary-used-percent`, `-primary-window-minutes`, `-primary-reset-at`, `-secondary-*`, `-limit-name` adjacent to `x-codex-active-limit`, `x-codex-credits-balance`, `x-codex-rate-limit-reached-type`.

There is also an **SSE variant** on the same stream: `parse_rate_limit_event()` in the same file consumes an event of `"type": "codex.rate_limits"` carrying `rate_limits.primary/secondary` (`used_percent`, `window_minutes`, `reset_at`), `credits`, and `plan_type`.

**Where Rhythm loses it:** `apps/opencode_fork/packages/opencode/src/plugin/codex.ts:408-485`. The plugin installs a custom `fetch` that attaches `Authorization: Bearer <token>` + `ChatGPT-Account-Id`, rewrites the URL to `CODEX_API_ENDPOINT = "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses"` (line 14), and `return fetch(url, {...init, headers})` — the `Response` goes straight to the AI SDK and **nobody reads `res.headers`**. The data is arriving on every Codex turn today and is discarded.

Caveat worth writing down: these header names do **not** contain the substring `ratelimit`, so any header filter keyed on that word silently drops them.

---

## 3. Line 2 — The Codex path: there is a plain, free GET

This is the recommendation. Codex CLI's own usage/status view does not probe the model; it calls a dedicated read-only endpoint.

`openai/codex` → `codex-rs/backend-client/src/client/rate_limit_resets.rs:124-129`:

```rust
fn rate_limit_status_url(&self) -> String {
    match self.path_style {
        PathStyle::CodexApi  => format!("{}/api/codex/usage", self.base_url),
        PathStyle::ChatGptApi => format!("{}/wham/usage", self.base_url),
    }
}
```

and `get_rate_limit_status()` (same file, ~line 68) issues `Method::GET` with `self.headers()`.

The base URL is normalized in `codex-rs/backend-client/src/client.rs:191-203` — `https://chatgpt.com` gets `/backend-api` appended and `PathStyle::ChatGptApi` selected. The upstream contract test pins it exactly (`rate_limit_resets_tests.rs`):

```rust
assert_eq!(
    test_client("https://chatgpt.com/backend-api", PathStyle::ChatGptApi).rate_limit_status_url(),
    "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage"
);
```

**The request.** From `client.rs:252-271` (`headers()`):

```
GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage
Authorization: Bearer <ChatGPT OAuth access token>
ChatGPT-Account-Id: <chatgpt_account_id>
User-Agent: codex-cli
```

**The response.** `RateLimitStatusWithResetCredits` (`backend-client/src/types.rs:56-67`) + the mock body in `rate_limit_resets_tests.rs`:

```json
{
  "plan_type": "plus",
  "rate_limit": {
    "allowed": true,
    "limit_reached": false,
    "primary_window":   { "used_percent": 41, "limit_window_seconds": 300,    "reset_after_seconds": 60, "reset_at": 2000000000 },
    "secondary_window": { "used_percent": 12, "limit_window_seconds": 604800, "reset_at": 2000600000 }
  },
  "credits": { "has_credits": true, "unlimited": false, "balance": "…" },
  "additional_rate_limits": [ { "metered_feature": "…", "limit_name": "…", "rate_limit": { } } ],
  "rate_limit_reset_credits": { "available_count": 3 },
  "account_id": "…", "user_id": "…"
}
```

Field→window mapping is `client.rs:642-648` (`primary_window` / `secondary_window`) and the window fields are `used_percent`, `limit_window_seconds`, `reset_after_seconds`, `reset_at`.

**Why this is the right one:**
- It is a `GET`. It sends no prompt, generates no tokens, and does not consume the 5h/weekly window it is reporting on — strictly cheaper than the Anthropic probe we already run every 60s.
- It maps 1:1 onto the existing `UsageBudgetProvider` shape: `kind: 'window'`, two items (`5h limit`, `weekly`), `remainingFraction = 1 - used_percent/100`, `resetAt = reset_at * 1000`, and `detail` from `plan_type` / credits balance — exactly the Anthropic block's shape, so `usage_budget.dart` and the panel need **zero** changes.
- The credential is already on disk and already refreshed. `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` holds an `openai` entry of `{type, refresh, access, expires}` (keys only — values not read or recorded), maintained by the opencode Codex plugin's refresh path (`codex.ts:428-447`).
- The one missing input, `ChatGPT-Account-Id`, is derivable locally with code that already exists in this repo: `extractAccountIdFromClaims()` at `apps/opencode_fork/packages/opencode/src/plugin/codex.ts:77-84` reads `chatgpt_account_id` (or `https://api.openai.com/auth.chatgpt_account_id`, or `organizations[0].id`) out of the JWT. Note the auth.json `openai` entry currently has **no** `accountId` key — the plugin only persists it on login/refresh — so the service must derive it from the token rather than assume it is stored.

**NOT CONFIRMED LIVE.** Per this session's credential rules I did not issue this request. Everything above is read off the CLI source and the installed binary. The single call needed to confirm shape-in-practice is the exact `GET` written out above; it costs no quota, but it is an authenticated request against the user's account, so it needs an explicit go-ahead.

---

## 4. Line 3 — Documented APIs: genuinely unusable here (the existing `reason` was right about this half)

- OpenAI's published usage/cost API is the **Admin** surface: `GET /v1/organization/usage/completions` and `GET /v1/organization/costs`. It requires an **Admin API key** (`sk-admin-…`), and admin keys cannot be used for non-administration endpoints. Refs: https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/admin/subresources/organization/subresources/usage/methods/costs and https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/completions_usage_api
- It reports **platform-organization** spend, which is a different ledger from a ChatGPT Plus/Pro plan's 5h/weekly Codex windows. Even with an admin key it would not answer "how much Codex do I have left".
- A ChatGPT-plan OAuth token is not a platform API key, so `api.openai.com` 401s it. That part of the current `reason` string stands and does not need re-testing.
- The only *official* human-facing surface for the plan windows is the web page `https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage` (string present in the installed binary) — a page, not an API.

---

## 5. Line 4 — Fallback: local accounting (not needed if §3 lands)

Available if §3 is rejected, but **weaker, and it must be labelled an estimate**:

- `agent_session_messages.tokens_json` exists (`apps/api_server/src/database/migrations.ts:1466`) and, per #1554, completed messages carry real `input`/`output`/cache counts.
- That yields "tokens spent in the last 5h / 7d", not "fraction remaining" — there is no local knowledge of the plan's ceiling, and the Codex windows are not a pure token count anyway.
- It would therefore have to render as `remainingFraction: null` with a `detail` string only (the shape `usage_budget.dart` already supports for pay-as-you-go OpenRouter). It must never be dressed up as a gauge.

Recommendation: do not build this. §3 is less code and is authoritative.

---

## Recommended approach

Add `fetchOpenAI(auth)` to `usage_budget_service.ts` alongside `fetchGemini` / `fetchOpenRouter`, and replace `openAiUnavailable()` in `buildSnapshot()`:

1. Read the `openai` entry from `auth.json` (already loaded by `readAuthJson()`). If `expires < Date.now()`, report `unavailable` and let the engine's own refresh fix it on the next Codex turn — simpler than duplicating the refresh flow in this service.
2. Derive `ChatGPT-Account-Id` from the access-token JWT claims (port `extractAccountIdFromClaims`).
3. `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage` with the three headers above, using the existing `PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` / `AbortSignal.timeout` pattern.
4. Map to `kind: 'window'` items `5h limit` and `weekly`; `remainingFraction = clamp(1 - used_percent/100)`; `resetAt` from `reset_at` (unix seconds — the existing `epochToIso()` helper already tolerates both s and ms); `detail` from `plan_type` and, when present, `credits.balance`.
5. Anything unexpected → the existing `{ kind: 'unavailable', reason }` path.

Second-order win: `agent_model_resolver.ts:545-560` downgrades a provider to the cheap tier when its lowest `remainingFraction` drops below `NEAR_BUDGET_REMAINING_THRESHOLD`. OpenAI is currently invisible to that logic (it fails open — `isProviderNearBudget` returns false for providers with no data), so Codex runs never get budget-aware routing. This fixes that for free.

---

## Fragility — read this before merging

`/backend-api/wham/usage` is **unofficial**. OpenAI publishes no reference page for it; the contract is inferred from the Codex CLI source and its own contract tests. It can change shape or disappear without notice, and it sits behind `chatgpt.com`, which can also serve an HTML challenge instead of JSON.

Non-negotiable failure posture — **a confidently wrong quota is worse than a blank one**:

- Validate before trusting. `used_percent` must be a finite number in `0..100`; `reset_at`, if present, must parse to a plausible instant. Anything else → `unavailable`.
- Verify the response is actually JSON (`content-type`), not an HTML interstitial. A body that does not parse → `unavailable`.
- Any non-2xx, timeout, missing `rate_limit` object, or missing `primary_window` → `unavailable` with the status in `reason`. **Never** substitute a default, never fall back to 0% or 100% used, never carry a stale value forward without saying so.
- Never invent a window the payload did not contain. If only `primary_window` comes back, emit one item, not two.
- Keep the existing 60s cache; a `GET` is cheap but not free of rate limiting.

When it breaks, the panel goes back to showing exactly what it shows today. That is the correct degradation.

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /agents/usage-budget` returns an `openai` provider with `kind: 'window'` and items `5h limit` + `weekly`, each with a `remainingFraction` in `0..1` and a parseable `resetAt`, when a valid ChatGPT-plan token is present.
- [ ] `remainingFraction` is derived as `1 - used_percent/100` and independently agrees with what `codex` itself reports for the same account at the same moment (manual cross-check).
- [ ] No new Flutter model or panel code is required — `usage_budget.dart` parses the new entry unchanged.
- [ ] The probe is a `GET` and sends no prompt; it does not consume the window it reports on.
- [ ] Unit tests cover, with mocked responses: happy path; non-2xx; HTML-instead-of-JSON; missing `rate_limit`; `primary_window` only; `used_percent` out of range or non-numeric; missing/expired token; missing account id. **Every one of these must produce `kind: 'unavailable'` with a reason — none may produce a number.**
- [ ] No token, refresh token, or account id is ever logged, and `reason` strings contain no credential material.
- [ ] #1566's expectation that OpenAI renders `unavailable` is updated.
- [ ] The stale second clause of the current `reason` string ("Codex usage backend is undocumented") is removed along with `openAiUnavailable()`.

## Out of scope

- Redeeming `rate-limit-reset-credits` (`POST /wham/rate-limit-reset-credits/consume`) — it exists and is adjacent, but spending a user's reset credit is not a usage-panel concern.
- Harvesting the `x-codex-*` headers off live Codex turns (§2). It is a valid second source and would be free/passive, but it only updates when a turn happens, so the panel would be stale on an idle app. Worth a follow-up only if `/wham/usage` proves unreliable.
trackingInterpretation: Research/proposal only, explicitly says no product code changed and requests revising #1566 unavailable expectation. Do not represent reachable OpenAI budget as implemented.

title: Unify model-picker visibility and availability filtering across providers
body:
## Summary

`GET /agents/models/catalog` does not apply one consistent visibility policy across direct and custom providers. The model picker can show stale or unwanted direct-provider models while omitting valid configured local models.

This is broader than completed issue #1143: custom providers can now appear, but provider-specific curation, authenticated-account availability, and built-in Ollama promotion remain inconsistent.

## Current behavior

- OpenAI exposes many stale/unwanted models instead of only the supported set:
  - `gpt-5.6-luna`
  - `gpt-5.6-terra`
  - `gpt-5.6-sol`
- Anthropic can expose older models rather than only the most recent currently available models (ideally the newest model in each active family).
- Gemini can expose models that are stale or unavailable to the authenticated account instead of only current chat models that account can use.
- Custom providers can retain old/unavailable entries. The desired configured custom set is:
  - `ollama-local-qwen`
  - `ollama-planner`
  - `ollama-executor`
- A valid Ollama model present in `opencode.json` and the engine catalog can still be absent from Rhythm's picker.
- Adding a custom provider to `opencode.json` may require a full boot before it is instantiated, even when `POST /config/reload` returns `true`.

## Architecture diagnosis

The model catalog route in `agents_models_routes` has visibility filtering only for OpenRouter. Built-in direct providers instead combine hard-coded fallback routes with live-model promotion, without a unified per-provider allowlist/visibility policy.

Built-in Ollama falls between the direct and custom paths:

- `isEligibleDirectModel` accepts prefixes for Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google, but rejects additional local Ollama models.
- `knownStaticProviderIds` includes Ollama, so Ollama is not handled through the custom-provider path either.

As a result, a model can exist in the engine catalog but remain absent from Rhythm's picker.

## Reproduction

1. Configure authenticated OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini providers plus Ollama/custom providers in `opencode.json`.
2. Include the desired custom entries `ollama-local-qwen`, `ollama-planner`, and `ollama-executor`, and ensure they are visible in the engine model catalog.
3. Start Rhythm and request `GET /agents/models/catalog`.
4. Observe stale/unwanted direct-provider models in the response.
5. Observe that an additional valid built-in Ollama model can be present in the engine catalog but missing from Rhythm's picker.
6. Add or change a custom provider, call `POST /config/reload`, and observe that a fresh boot may still be required before the provider is instantiated and reflected in the picker.

## Expected behavior

Rhythm should apply one explicit per-provider visibility mechanism to both built-in direct providers and custom providers, intersected with models actually available to the authenticated account. Live-model promotion should work for built-in Ollama instead of excluding valid configured local models.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unified per-provider allowlist/visibility mechanism governs direct and custom provider entries returned by `/agents/models/catalog`.
- [ ] OpenAI returns only `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, and `gpt-5.6-sol`.
- [ ] Anthropic returns only the most recent currently available models, preferably the newest model per active family.
- [ ] Gemini returns only current chat models available to the authenticated account.
- [ ] Custom providers return only configured, available entries; for the current configuration that is `ollama-local-qwen`, `ollama-planner`, and `ollama-executor`.
- [ ] Built-in Ollama live-model promotion admits eligible configured Ollama models instead of dropping them between the direct and custom paths.
- [ ] Removed, stale, or unavailable models do not remain visible through hard-coded fallbacks.
- [ ] Reload semantics are explicit and correct: either `POST /config/reload` instantiates newly added providers, or the API/UI clearly reports that a full restart is required.
- [ ] Coverage exercises direct-provider curation, account-aware filtering, custom-provider filtering, built-in Ollama promotion, and config reload/fresh-boot behavior.

## Related

- #1143 addressed custom OpenAI-compatible providers being entirely absent from the picker; this issue covers the remaining cross-provider curation and promotion architecture.
trackingInterpretation: Open issue explicitly says #1143 is narrower/completed and provider curation/account availability/Ollama promotion remain inconsistent. Do not count #1143 as full model-picker parity.

title: Routed model aliases break provenance: only openrouter/free is recorded, never the model that actually ran
body:
## Symptom

When a session runs against a **router alias** rather than a concrete model, Rhythm records only the alias. The model that actually produced the work is never captured, so the session record cannot answer "what wrote this code?"

## Evidence (observed live, 2026-09-21)

Two agents dispatched with `{"providerID":"openrouter","modelID":"openrouter/free"}` — OpenRouter's auto-router, which selects an underlying free model per request and fails over between providers.

Both completed successfully (19m36s / 62 steps, and 18m50s / 36 steps). Across **98 message records**, every single one stored the alias:

```
62 "modelID":"openrouter/free"  "providerID":"openrouter"   (session df873dbe-…)
36 "modelID":"openrouter/free"  "providerID":"openrouter"   (session 0210dcc7-…)
```

Not one record names a resolved model. The upstream generation IDs that would allow querying OpenRouter after the fact are not stored either, so the information is unrecoverable once the run ends.

## Why this matters

Rhythm treats provenance and the audit trail as load-bearing. A routed dispatch is a hole in that record:

1. **Review has no subject.** A run can pass verification with no durable evidence of what produced it. "This was written by `openrouter/free`" names a routing policy, not a model.
2. **It is silently non-reproducible.** The same alias resolves differently tomorrow — by design, since the whole point of the router is failover. Two runs with identical inputs and identical recorded metadata can come from different models.
3. **Quality signals cannot be attributed.** In tonight's comparison, the `openrouter/free` run on #1558 produced a fake acceptance contract: six placeholder `expect(false).toBe(true)` tests, reported as "confirmed failing." That is a serious quality finding, and it currently cannot be attributed to any model — only to a router.
4. **The same gap will apply to any aggregator.** This is not OpenRouter-specific; it affects any provider that resolves an alias server-side.

## Where the data exists

OpenRouter attributes each generation to a concrete model and exposes it on the generation record. The response metadata for a chat completion includes the resolved model, and `GET /api/v1/generation?id=…` returns full attribution — but only if the generation ID is retained.

So this is a capture problem, not an availability problem.

## Proposed change

- On each assistant message, record the **resolved** model alongside the requested one — something like `requestedModelId` (`openrouter/free`) and `resolvedModelId` (whatever actually served).
- Persist the upstream generation ID per step where the provider supplies one, so attribution can be reconstructed later.
- Surface the distinct set of resolved models on the session record, so a reviewer can see at a glance that a run spanned N different models.

## Open questions

- Should a routed alias be **disallowed** for runs that are expected to pass a verification gate, or merely flagged? An argument exists for "review requires a named model."
- Should the session summary warn when a single run spanned multiple resolved models, since that changes how its output should be read?
- Is there an engine-side hook that already surfaces the resolved model, or does this need the provider response metadata threaded through the stream bridge?

## Context

Found while extending a model-comparison run to free-tier providers. Full writeup lives with that comparison; the relevant sessions are `df873dbe-b785-4bbd-9e1b-3c9ffebdff9f` and `0210dcc7-7897-4cb5-be51-1f20a4453cdd`.

Related: the workdir/worktree dispatch issue filed alongside this one, found in the same run.
trackingInterpretation: Open issue has observed alias-only provenance and unrecoverable missing request IDs; separate routed-model provenance from mere selected-alias display.

title: Transcript child-chip grid fix (#1552) + persisted project-group collapse (#1558) — network Qwen
body:
Two frontend fixes implemented by **network Qwen 3.8 27B** (`ollama-planner`, self-hosted) during the 2026-09-21 model-comparison run. Both were produced in isolated worktrees off `main` (`648f8d58`), with acceptance contracts written before implementation.

Closes #1552. Closes #1558.

---

## #1552 — delegated-task card grid regression

**Two independent defects, both in `apps/web/src/styles.css` (lines 289–290):**

1. `.child-chip` declared **3** grid tracks (`8px minmax(0, 1fr) 14px`) for a button with **2** children. The title `<span>` was parked in the 8px track and wrapped one word per line; the chevron floated mid-card in the `1fr` track.
2. `.child-chip > span:nth-child(2)` targeted the **chevron SVG** (the 2nd child), never the content span — so the span never became a grid container and title/meta ran together.

Fix is two selector/track edits, no abstraction:

```diff
- grid-template-columns: 8px minmax(0, 1fr) 14px;
+ grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 14px;
- .child-chip > span:nth-child(2) { display: grid; }
+ .child-chip > span:nth-child(1) { display: grid; }
```

### ⚠️ This supersedes an earlier incomplete fix

During the same comparison run, **Claude Haiku 4.5 produced a fix for #1552 that addressed only the second defect** (`nth-child(2)` → `nth-child(1)`) and left the 3-track declaration in place. That leaves the title still parked in the 8px track — **the card is still visibly broken.**

Haiku's 5 contract tests passed anyway, because they asserted on the stylesheet and DOM structure rather than measuring rendered geometry. Qwen caught it explicitly:

> "The haiku sibling that fixed only `nth-child(2)→(1)` left the title in the 8px track — still broken. Both are fixed here, as the issue body and dispatch require."

If any Haiku-authored #1552 branch is still open, **close it in favour of this one.** GPT-5.6 Luna's #1552 attempt has the same single-defect limitation.

### Verification approach

The contract spec here renders the **real fixture-mode app** and measures the **actual `.child-chip`** at 1440 / 1024 / 780, rather than asserting on stylesheet text. That difference is why it caught what the other two missed. Rendered evidence is committed at `docs/ai/runs/artifacts/issue-1552/evidence/child-chip-1440.png` (captured by the test under `RHYTHM_CAPTURE_EVIDENCE=1`).

Contract: 6 criteria (c1–c5 automated, c6 manual), RED and GREEN both recorded in the run log.

---

## #1558 — collapsed / persisted project groups

Replaces the non-persisted `collapsedProjects` / `new Set()` state in `SessionRail.tsx` with a persisted **open-projects** set (`rhythm-agents-projects-open`), mirroring the try/catch localStorage pattern already present in `store.tsx` rather than introducing a parallel convention.

The inversion is deliberate: with "all collapsed" as the default, an open-set stays small and a project that has never been touched needs no entry at all.

Behaviour:

- Fresh load defaults every project group collapsed
- The selected session's group expands
- Toggle survives reload and remount
- State is per project id; new projects don't disturb existing entries
- Corrupt or unavailable storage falls back safely
- Existing chevron and `aria-expanded` behaviour unchanged

Ships a 6-case Playwright contract **plus a Node-runnable mirror** (`.test.mjs`) so the gate stays observable without a browser — useful given the harness trouble documented below.

---

**No agent in this run produced live runtime evidence.** Every agent hit the sandbox executable-identity guard, and none bypassed it (correctly — the guard was treated as a verification blocker, not an obstacle to route around).

So both changes here rest on **test-level evidence only**:

- #1552 — contract RED before, GREEN after; rendered screenshot captured
- #1558 — contract RED (c1–c5) before, 6/6 GREEN after; TypeScript clean for `SessionRail.tsx`

The full project typecheck reports 395 cascade errors, all `Cannot find module 'react'` from an empty `node_modules` — environmental, confirmed unrelated.

**Recommend a manual smoke in the running app before merge**, particularly for #1558's persistence across a real restart.

Both implementations are the work of `qwen3.8:27b-mlx` served from the network Ollama host, dispatched through Rhythm's async delegation with acceptance-contract-first discipline. It was the strongest performer of six agents across three model families on these two issues — the only one to write a browser-independent test mirror, to reason about why a passing criterion was *legitimately* passing rather than falsely green, and to correctly identify environmental noise instead of reporting it as failure.

Work from the other models in that run is deliberately **not** included here.
