title: feat(agents): prompt an existing agent session over HTTP + MCP
body:
## What's missing today

There is no way to send a prompt into an **existing** Rhythm agent session programmatically:

- `POST /agent-sessions/:id/resume` takes no prompt
- `POST /agent-sessions` creates a session, it can't prompt one
- `/message-threads/:id/messages` is the human messaging system, not agent input
- Agent prompts go over the WebSocket gateway, which only the app UI drives

So an external caller can spawn *children* under an orchestrator via `POST /agent-delegation/delegate-async`, but can't give the orchestrator itself any instruction. Concretely: a live orchestrator whose children have just finished has to be told "review this and open a PR" by hand, in the app.

## What this adds

`POST /agent-sessions/:id/prompt` → 202, exposed as MCP tool `rhythm_prompt_session`. Plus `GET /agent-sessions/:id/prompt-log`.

The endpoint delegates to **`handleInputFrame`** — the WS gateway's own `session.input` handler — passing a shim that captures the error frames it would have written to a socket and turns them into a 502. That handler is ~400 lines of per-turn behaviour: profile scope, MCP and skill allowlists, model resolution, auto-resume, memory/skill prefaces, experiment enrollment. Re-implementing any of it here would guarantee the programmatic path drifts from the composer path. Auto-resume comes free — prompting a `resumable` session wakes it.

## Cloudflare or the agent API? — the agent API, and it can't be otherwise

Production (`api.vcrcapps.com`) holds none of the state a prompt needs. The opencode engine, the in-process `opencodeSessionMap`, the stream bridge and the SQLite `agent_sessions` rows all live in the desktop-embedded server on **:4001**. A Cloudflare-side route would have nothing to prompt.

The contrast with `claude-triggers` is the useful one: that path stays on production because it is *delivery* — `AgentTriggerWatcher` polls prod and hands the trigger to the local server. Execution has always been local. This endpoint is execution, so it's local, and the MCP tool is registered at `RHYTHM_AGENT_URL` like every other local-agent-server tool.

## Auth: flat, by design

**Any running session is promptable. No parentage check.** The Rhythm API/MCP secret key is the trust boundary. Gating on parentage would block the main use case — a caller prompting a session it didn't create.

I read the `#1322` comment on `callerSessionId` before writing this. Its lesson is about *identity provenance* — a model asked for its own Rhythm session id invents a plausible UUID scraped from its cwd, so the MCP layer supplies the engine session id from trusted context instead. That lesson is kept: `callerSdkSessionId` still comes from trusted context, never from the model. What is **not** kept is using it to decide *whether* a call is allowed. Here it feeds the audit row only; it authorizes nothing.

## The audit trail, because the key isn't the threat model

The key doesn't defend against prompt injection — a compromised agent holds it legitimately. An agent that reads a GitHub issue body containing "send this instruction to session X" is making an authorized call with someone else's words. Indistinguishable from a legitimate call at the auth layer; obvious in a log. **Logging, not gating.**

- `agent_prompt_injections`: target, caller session, caller engine session, caller user, source, full prompt, accepted/error, timestamp.
- Written **before** dispatch — an injection that crashes the dispatch path is exactly the one worth having — then settled with the outcome.
- **Append-only**: a `BEFORE DELETE` trigger aborts. A compromised caller can't erase its own row.
- SQLite-only, no Postgres twin (local agent server is the sole writer, like `agent_session_messages`).

This pairs with open issue #1576 (routed models break provenance) — the same provenance gap, on a different path.

Belt and braces: `rhythm_prompt_session` also sits behind the existing outbound approval gate as a new `session.prompt` action, which bites once the calling session has actually consumed untrusted content — the same posture as `rhythm_delegate_async`.

## Checks

- `tsc --noEmit` clean, both `api_server` and `mcp_server`
- `apps/mcp_server` vitest: **188 passed**, 2 skipped
- `apps/api_server` vitest (non-live): **6104 passed**, 27 skipped, **1 failed** — `workflow_failure_signal_extractor.test.ts > stale-redo`. Pre-existing full-suite flake: passes in isolation both with and without this branch, and touches none of the files here. Not investigated further.
- New `issue_1577_prompt_existing_session.test.ts` (4 tests): the prompt actually reaches `promptAsync`; the audit row attributes an **unrelated** caller, so a regression toward parentage-gating fails here; an empty prompt 400s without dispatching or auditing; the delete trigger fires; `prompt-log` serves it.

**No live smoke.** Session `325e03e3` is a live orchestrator with in-flight children and the running :4001 server is the old build — restarting it to test would have disturbed it. The test drives the real Express app end to end instead.

## Notes

- PR #1544 is an open draft on this same base branch.
- Not addressed here: #1575 (child sessions inherit the manager's cwd; the dispatcher doesn't pass an absolute workdir).
- Don't merge — leaving open for your review and local testing.

title: Electron session window: adopt OpenCode Desktop chat streaming, including live thinking and readable timestamps
body:
## Problem

The Electron session/chat window is buggy and does not stream the agent's reasoning/thinking as it happens. Message timestamps are rendered as raw ISO strings and are difficult to read.

`apps/web/src/components/Transcript.tsx` currently renders reasoning only when a mapped `reasoning` block exists and prints `message.createdAt` verbatim. The app already receives `message.part.updated` and `message.part.delta` events, but the user-visible session surface does not match the robust live transcript behavior of OpenCode Desktop.

## Reuse before rebuilding

First evaluate whether Rhythm can directly reuse or thinly adapt the vendored OpenCode Desktop session/message components and state reducer. Relevant references include:

- `apps/opencode_fork/packages/app/src/pages/session.tsx`
- OpenCode global-sync message/part state and event reduction
- `apps/opencode_fork/packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run/session-data.ts`
- `apps/opencode_fork/packages/opencode/test/cli/run/session-data.test.ts`

The proven reducer handles delayed role discovery, reasoning/text deltas, tools, interruption, errors and ordering. Prefer sharing/adapting that behavior over writing another parallel transcript engine. If direct component reuse is impractical because of Solid/React boundaries, port the smallest stable message/part reducer and preserve its event semantics.

Existing focused defects #1553 and #1554 remain separate. Coordinate timestamp formatting with #1565 instead of inventing another formatter.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reasoning/thinking text appears incrementally from live reasoning deltas while the agent works; it is not delayed until the final REST reload.
- [ ] Delayed `message.part.updated` snapshots do not erase reasoning/text already assembled from deltas.
- [ ] Text, reasoning, tool start/progress/final/error, permissions, questions, compaction and interruption preserve engine order and update one stable message/part instead of duplicating rows.
- [ ] A provider/model that does not expose reasoning shows no fake empty thinking block.
- [ ] Thinking is readable but visually subordinate, collapsible when long, and preserves user expand/collapse state while streaming.
- [ ] Switching sessions and returning restores the live/final transcript without duplicated or missing parts.
- [ ] Scroll behavior matches OpenCode Desktop: pinned readers follow growth; readers who scrolled up keep position/focus and receive a visible new-output affordance.
- [ ] Message timestamps use the shared local-time formatter: concise time for recent messages, date + time when needed, machine-readable `dateTime`, and accessible full timestamp text/tooltip. Raw ISO strings never render as the visible label.
- [ ] Invalid/missing timestamps degrade to an honest fallback without breaking the transcript.
- [ ] Focused reducer tests replay real OpenCode event sequences, including reasoning delta before snapshot, interrupted turns and session errors.
- [ ] Playwright evidence shows live thinking changing before turn completion and readable timestamps.
- [ ] Final qualification runs against the real engine in the isolated sandbox; a mocked WebSocket alone is insufficient.

## Likely files

- `apps/web/src/components/Transcript.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/store.tsx` live event reduction/mapping
- `apps/web/src/gateway/sessions.ts`
- `apps/web/tests/electron-e52a-transcript.spec.ts`
- shared timestamp formatter from #1565
- selected vendored OpenCode Desktop message/part utilities if reusable without pulling unrelated UI

## Constraints

Do not fork/copy the entire OpenCode application into Rhythm. Reuse one maintained component/reducer boundary or port the minimum event semantics with attribution and focused tests. Keep permission/security boundaries and Rhythm-specific child-session navigation intact.
trackingInterpretation: Open issue explicitly combines live reasoning streaming and human-readable timestamps; work on #1553/#1554 may partially address reasoning, while #1565 separately confirms Electron timestamp gap. Full acceptance is still open.

title: Local decision engine: Auto (router) sessions, model/tool/memory ranking, capacity routing, router settings
body:
## Summary

This adds a local decision engine to `apps/api_server`, built on the "typed decision + confidence" idea behind TypeSafe Jev, plus the UI to use it. Nothing changes for existing sessions; new sessions default to **Auto (router)** in **shadow** mode until the router is calibrated.

**Engine (`services/decision/`)**
- Reranker client for `POST /v1/rerank` (llama.cpp, TEI, Jina, Cohere shapes) plus a Jev client (`/v1/systemone`, one yes/no Choice question per candidate).
- `rankCandidates` and `classify`; a local-only `agent_decision_log` table (capped at 20k rows; no-op on Postgres); `GET /agent-decisions` with agreement, latency and calibration stats.
- **Router backend settings:** `GET/PUT /agent-decisions/config` and `POST /config/test`. Local / Jev / custom (LAN or other server). API keys are write-only (0600 file). Jev and non-loopback servers require an explicit data-sharing consent. Env vars still win and show as locked in the UI.

**The router chooses only among models enabled in Rhythm**
- Candidates = the models explicitly enabled in Models curation (`agent_model_visibility`) ∩ connected ∩ eligible ∩ entitled ∩ not excluded in Router settings. No static approved list is consulted by the router; the picker route and the catalog share one `loadModelVisibility()` so they cannot drift.
- Nothing curated → the router keeps each chat's baseline model and logs `no_curated_models`. `ROUTE_FALLBACKS_BY_AGENT` is used only when the engine is unreachable, and the decision log says so.
- `providerSnapshot()` now passes through `cost`, `releaseDate`, `family`, `reasoning`.
- Tiers derive from output price over the curated set. `tiers.mode: auto` (default) places the two cutoffs at the largest log-price gaps among the newest model per family (real models.dev prices: ≈$7.75 / ≈$19.4 per M → haiku/mini/flash cheap, sonnet/gpt-5.4/codex/gemini-pro standard, opus/gpt-5.5 frontier). `manual` takes explicit values; per-model overrides and exclusions are honoured.
- Within a tier: base provider (keeps account + prompt cache) → most usage headroom → lowest output cost → newest release. gpt-5.5-pro ($180) never wins frontier over opus/gpt-5.5.

**Features (each off / shadow / on)**
- **Model routing:** classifies the prompt as cheap / standard / frontier, then picks from the curated catalog. Never overrides a turn, session or profile pin.
- **Routing scope:** `first_prompt` (default: one pick per session, persisted), `escalate_only` (only moves up a tier at ≥0.75 confidence), `every_prompt`.
- **Tool ranking:** reorders MCP servers by relevance and defers low scorers (still granted via `mcp_dispatch`; the grant set never shrinks).
- **Memory ranking:** reranks an owner-scoped pool (16 × 700 chars) including Engraph rank-only hits; owner/lifecycle gates and caps unchanged.
- **Capacity routing:** reads the cached usage snapshot (self-primed in the background, 5-minute floor). Picks the account with the most headroom; when the base provider is low, moves to an equivalent tier on another provider (by price band, from the curated catalog); when all are low, lowest capable tier then most headroom. Only auto-picked sessions can switch accounts.

**Auto (router) session mode**
- `agent_sessions.model_mode` (`auto` | `fixed`; column default `fixed`, interactive POST defaults `auto`). An echoed `modelOverride` equal to the stored/profile model no longer pins the session.
- Auto sessions run model routing and capacity routing in **shadow** unless the feature is set to On in Router settings (an explicit env `off` is a kill switch).
- **Mobile** prompts are routed in the OpenCode proxy (`prompt_async` body `model` rewrite), so no engine change is needed; the relay path inherits it.

**UI**
- **Electron (`apps/web`):** "Auto (router)" first in the Composer model picker, an "Auto → <model>" status from model-provenance, and a Router model card in Agent Settings → Models: backend, per-feature modes, consent, test connection, and a **"Models the router chooses among"** table (curation state, tier override, $/M, release date, exclude) with Auto/Manual cutoffs.
- **Mobile:** Auto in the session picker (prompts omit `model`), an "Auto → <model>" label, and the same Router model section (including the catalog table) in Settings.
- **Flutter:** Auto in the unified picker; first-message guard relaxed for auto sessions.

**Tooling**
- `scripts/decision_bench.ts`: fixtures for all three ranking features (accuracy, recall@3, MRR, nDCG, ECE, latency).
- `scripts/decision_calibrate.ts`: 20 labelled prompts → per-prompt picks, confusion matrix, a min-confidence threshold sweep with a recommendation, over/under-routing counts, and tier-description diagnostics. Both use the live catalog for expected models when the engine is reachable (`--static-catalog` to force the table).

## Why this change

Model tier, tool surface and memory injection are hand-coded heuristics today; the Engraph semantic lane is effectively disabled (no calibrated confidence); account limits were only handled after a 429; and the model route table was generations out of date. This tries the decision-model approach on local open weights first, chooses only among the models the user has enabled, and ships shadow logging plus a calibration script so it can be measured before anything is switched on.

## Scope boundaries

- **Intended area:** intentionally multi-area — `backend` (`apps/api_server`), `desktop` (`apps/web`, `apps/desktop_flutter`), mobile (`apps/mobile`), plus `docs/ai/` logs as CLAUDE.md requires.
- **Explicitly out of scope:** changes to the OpenCode fork; a hosted backend other than Jev; tool ranking at `agent_runner` session creation (no prompt available there).
- `tools/git/check_pr_scope.sh` flags cross-area files by design (see above).

## Acceptance criteria checklist
- [x] Requirements implemented (routing among the curated catalog, tool/memory ranking, capacity routing, Auto default, router settings on desktop + mobile, first-prompt scope, calibration test)
- [x] Architecture boundaries preserved (logic in `services/decision/*`, thin try/catch integrations, thin controllers)
- [x] Docs updated (`docs/ai/decision-engine-setup.md`, plan, decision, run, project-state)
- [x] Tests added across all layers (see below)
- [x] PR diff reviewed for unrelated files

## Testing

- **api_server:** `tsc --noEmit` clean; the decision (incl. `model_catalog*`), memory, routing, sessions, ws_gateway, runner, mobile, provider-catalog, agents_models and migration suites pass (1100+ tests). Regression tests: the router chooses models that are NOT in `ROUTE_FALLBACKS_BY_AGENT`; a policy-listed model with no curation row is NOT routable, an explicitly enabled one is; empty curation keeps the baseline; derived cutoffs run against real models.dev prices. Full-suite failures not caused by this PR (verified on the base): `w1_corrective_6_lifecycle` (root ignores chmod), 3 × `issue_1186` (`sandbox.sh`), and the scheduler boot-timing tests (`issue_1214`, `issue_1222`, `config_doctor_run_history`) that fail only on a loaded runner and pass locally / on re-run.
- **web:** `tsc -b` clean; Playwright contract spec passes; existing issue-1580 model-curation (29) and fixture-mode composer specs (13) pass.
- **mobile:** `tsc --noEmit` clean; settings/chat jest suites pass; e2e `foundation` suite green after updating two specs for the Auto default. Pre-existing failures verified on the base: 4 × `issue-1387`, 1 × `issue-1173`.
- **desktop_flutter:** `dart format` applied; `flutter analyze` at baseline (319 infos, 0 errors/warnings); 740 tests pass; the 2 golden failures are pre-existing Linux rendering diffs.
- `decision_bench.ts --fake` and `decision_calibrate.ts --fake` run end to end.
- **Not yet run against a real reranker or Jev.** The Jev request shape is taken from third-party docs (the official docs are blocked from this container); the Test-connection button will show immediately if a field name is off. Next step on a Mac: enable the models you want in Models curation, start `llama-server --reranking` with Qwen3-Reranker, run `scripts/decision_calibrate.ts`, check the catalog table in Router settings, adjust the threshold or `TIER_LABELS`, then set Model routing to On.
- GitNexus tools were unavailable in this session; blast radius was assessed by hand.
